takeaway: Type I (immediate) hypersensitivity is mediated by IgE: CD4+ Th2 cells stimulate B cells to make allergen-specific IgE. Examples: allergic asthma, anaphylaxis.

lines.text: Type One hypersensitivity is an immediate, allergic reaction.
It is provoked by re-exposure to a specific antigen, called an allergen.
CD4+ Th2 cells stimulate B cells to produce IgE antibodies specific to that antigen.
